title: Managing Franchise Agreement Risk with Franchise ERP E-Contracts
description: Understand Korea's 14-day franchise review period, when it shortens to 7 days, and how FDAM's e-contracts automate documents, delivery logs and contract dates.
html:
The 14-day review period for franchise agreements, the conditions for shortening it to 7 days, and how to manage it safely with e-contracts

franchise agreement, Franchise Business Act, pre-contract disclosure documents, e-contract, 14-day review period, franchise consultant advice, franchise ERP, FDAM, HQ sales management, franchise store management software

Key takeaways

· Korea's Franchise Business Act allows franchise fees to be collected and agreements to be signed only after 14 days have passed since the franchise disclosure document was provided.

· If the prospective franchisee has received advice from a lawyer or a certified franchise consultant, the review period is shortened to 7 days.

· Manual management based on Excel and paper documents is a major cause of scheduling errors and dispute risk.

· FDAM ties automatic document generation, secure delivery, viewing history and automatic date calculation into a single flow, reducing both sales and legal risk.

Managing franchise agreement riskstarts with strictly observing the 14-day review period set by the Franchise Business Act. A franchisor may not collect franchise fees or sign a franchise agreement until 14 days have passed from the date it provided the franchise disclosure document to the prospective franchisee, and violating this period can lead to fines or corrective orders. The more successful an HQ's sales efforts, the more consultations and contracts it has in progress, and the harder this rule becomes to manage.

On the other hand, if the prospective franchisee has received advice on the franchise disclosure document from a lawyer or a certified franchise consultant, the review period is shortened to 7 days. In other words, there is a lawful way to speed up business while staying compliant. In this post, we explain how to handle this flow with a system instead of Excel, through the sales management workflow of FDAM, the ERP from MS Venter, which has focused on franchise IT for nearly 25 years.

E-contracts are the most practical starting point for reducing franchise agreement risk.

1. The limits of manual Excel management, from document creation to date calculation

Manual contract management is a major source of legal risk and inefficiency.

The first step in franchise agreement work is preparing pre-contract disclosure documentssuch as the franchise disclosure document and a statement of nearby franchise stores. Many HQs create these documents manually each time a new prospective owner comes along, copying an existing Excel file and changing only the name and date. Along the way, typos creep in, and outdated versions of the franchise disclosure document are sometimes sent out by mistake.

The bigger problem is calculating the review period.

"This one got advice, so it's 7 days; that one didn't, so it's 14…"

When staff count days on a calendar one case at a time, being off by a day or two can mean breaking the law or missing the earliest signing date and losing a sales opportunity. Contract management that relies on human memory becomes a bigger risk as HQ expands its franchise business.

2. Automatic generation and secure delivery of pre-contract disclosure documents in one click

FDAM supports everything from document generation and delivery to logging viewing history in one place.

FDAM dramatically cuts time spent on tedious paperwork. It automatically generates tailored pre-contract disclosure documents for each prospective owner based on the latest franchise disclosure document data registered in the system, so HQ sales staff no longer need to copy and edit files every time.

Features of FDAM's electronic document delivery system

· Secure link delivery — A unique secure link for each prospective franchisee is sent via KakaoTalk, email or text message.

· Viewing time logged — The moment a prospective franchisee clicks the link and opens the documents, the viewing date and time are recorded on the server.

· Delivery date confirmed — This reduces the risk of "I never received the documents" disputes, and the review period countdown starts automatically from this point.

Viewing history isn't just a convenience feature; it is the basis for calculating the 14-day review period under the Franchise Business Act and, should a dispute arise later, HQ's strongest piece of evidence.

3. Cut the contract timeline to 7 days with a lawyer/franchise consultant advice check

Check the advice box, and the earliest signing date automatically shortens from 14 days to 7.

This is the heart of FDAM's contract management. Going beyond a simple document delivery tool, FDAM builds the Franchise Business Act's shortening conditions into its system logic. It's the result of taking the points where HQ sales staff most often make mistakes, as seen in our work with about 500 brands, and translating them directly into the system.

A safe, system-driven process for shortening the timeline

① Advice check — When sending the documents, staff check [Advised by a lawyer or franchise consultant].

② Automatic date calculation — The system automatically shortens the review period from 14 days to 7 and resets the "earliest signing date (D-Day)."

③ System control — The "Sign contract" step stays disabled until the calculated date arrives, preventing at the system level the illegal situation of collecting franchise fees or signing an agreement before the legally required period ends.

Staff no longer have to count days on a calendar and can spend their time on what really matters: caring for prospective franchisees and improving consultation quality.

4. E-contract integration and turning data into an asset

Once the review period has passed, the main agreement is executed through the e-contract system integrated with FDAM. Because prospective franchisee information accumulated during sales management carries straight over into the contract stage, there's no need to enter the same information twice.

  • One-stop process — Automatic document generation → secure delivery and advice check → period-elapsed alert → e-contract signing, all connected in one flow.
  • Turning data into an asset — Signed contract data is converted into "store master data" within the ERP and used immediately as the baseline data for opening preparation and logistics setup.

Just ask the FDAM AI assistant, which was the first to be built into a Korean franchise ERP, "Show me this month's missing pre-contract disclosure documents," and it organizes cases that haven't met the 14-day review period, unviewed documents and unsent documents into a table. HQ executives can quickly check the status and make decisions right before a meeting.

5. Results: reducing HQ sales and legal risk together

HQs that wanted to aggressively increase new store openings but were losing time to date-calculation errors and registered-mail paperwork due to the limits of Excel management typically see the following after adopting FDAM.

Typical changes after adoption

· Shorter contract lead times — Using the lawyer/franchise consultant advice check, eligible cases can have their waiting period reduced to 7 days, moving signing dates forward.

· Legal certainty — Thanks to the system's date controls, mistakes such as review period violations are blocked at the system level.

· Greater efficiency — Freed from registered mail and manual schedule management, the sales team can focus on caring for prospective franchisees.

Speed matters in franchise agreements, but above all, procedural legitimacyis everything. FDAM is a system that naturally builds into HQ sales staff's everyday workflow an environment for signing contracts as quickly and safely as the law allows.

Frequently asked questions

Q. What exactly is the 14-day review period under the Franchise Business Act?

It is a rule under the Franchise Business Act that prohibits a franchisor from collecting franchise fees or signing a franchise agreement until 14 days have passed from the date it provided the franchise disclosure document to the prospective franchisee. Violating this period can result in fines or corrective orders.

Q. When is it shortened to 7 days?

The review period is shortened from 14 days to 7 only when the prospective franchisee has received advice on the franchise disclosure document from a lawyer or a certified franchise consultant. HQ cannot shorten the period at its own discretion, and the advice must be confirmed.

Q. Is electronic delivery history accepted as legal evidence?

The Franchise Business Act allows pre-contract disclosure documents to be provided in writing or electronically, and when the system logs the viewing date and time, that record can be used to calculate the 14-day review period and as evidence in disputes.

Q. Does FDAM's e-contract feature require adopting a separate solution?

Within its sales management module, FDAM provides automatic generation of pre-contract disclosure documents, secure delivery, viewing history and automatic date calculation in a single flow. The main agreement is executed through an integrated e-contract system, so HQ doesn't need to run an additional separate solution.
